topic_and_scope: Development and external validation of an end-to-end machine learning model for predicting hospital-acquired pressure injuries (HAPI) using raw, time-series EMR data across multiple hospitals, with comparison to the Braden Scale and emphasis on EMR integration for real-time risk scoring.
main_themes: End-to-end EMR-integrated HAPI risk prediction using time-series data
Temporal dynamics and feature engineering to capture evolving patient risk while avoiding reliance on length of stay
Generalizability, implementation challenges, and clinician workflow integration for diverse health systems
main_findings: A time-series XGBoost model achieved AUROC values around 0.83–0.85 across internal and external validation cohorts and demonstrated superior performance to the Braden Scale in sensitivity and F1-score across multiple facilities.

An automated labeling pipeline leveraging wound care expert criteria achieved 98% labeling accuracy, enabling scalable, end-to-end EMR data processing for model training and potential continuous learning.

key_gaps.description: External validation in diverse health systems beyond Mount Sinai NYC to assess generalizability across settings with different patient populations and documentation practices.

Reliance on WOCN-derived labeling for ground truth and potential variability when deployed in settings with limited wound-care expertise or different documentation practices; need robust labeling compatible with RN workflows.

future_directions.title: Expand external validation to diverse health systems and geographies
future_directions.rationale: To determine the model's generalizability across non-academic and non-New York hospitals with varying patient demographics and documentation practices. This should involve collecting multi-institution datasets with standardized label definitions, evaluating AUROC, calibration, and decision-curve metrics, and adapting the pipeline to different EHR configurations. Steps include establishing data-sharing agreements, harmonizing labeling criteria, and conducting prospective validation in at least three distinct health systems over 12–24 months.

future_directions.title: Pilot real-time deployment as EHR-integrated decision support and assess impact on HAPI incidence
future_directions.rationale: Implementation in specific units (e.g., general wards, step-down units) to measure real-world effectiveness on patient outcomes, workflow integration, and acceptance by nurses and clinicians. Next steps: deploy the model in a controlled pilot, monitor alert utilization, track changes in prevention actions (repositioning frequency, skin assessments), and quantify changes in HAPI incidence, time-to-intervention, and resource use over 6–12 months.

future_directions.title: Integrate multimodal data (unstructured notes and imaging) to further improve predictive performance
future_directions.rationale: The current model relies on structured time-series data; incorporating unstructured progress notes through NLP and imaging data (e.g., wound photos) via computer vision could capture additional risk signals. Concrete steps: develop NLP pipelines to extract temporal features from notes, create imaging-derived skin integrity metrics, fuse modalities with the time-series model, and evaluate incremental AUROC and calibration improvements in retrospective and prospective analyses.

future_directions.title: Evolve labeling strategy to reduce dependence on wound-care experts
future_directions.rationale: Manual WOCN labeling is resource-intensive and may limit scalability across diverse settings. Develop semi-supervised and active learning approaches, incorporate RN-friendly labeling workflows, and validate labeling accuracy across sites to minimize drift. Actions include creating an RN-aligned labeling protocol, implementing active learning to prioritize uncertain cases, and monitoring label accuracy and model performance during deployment.

future_directions.title: Assess cross-EHR portability and adapt data pipelines for different platforms
future_directions.rationale: To ensure broader adoption, evaluate performance with data from various EHR systems (beyond Epic/Cerner) and across hospitals with heterogeneous data models. Implement standardized data extraction adapters, perform re-training or transfer learning as needed, and compare performance and calibration across platforms to identify system-specific adjustments.

future_directions.title: Define clinically actionable risk thresholds and reporting formats for nurses
future_directions.rationale: Calibrate risk thresholds and risk-category outputs to balance sensitivity and specificity in real-world workflows, and design concise, interpretable risk summaries suitable for RN decision-making. Steps: conduct threshold-tuning studies within multiple units, implement tiered alerts (e.g., high/medium/low risk), and evaluate impact on workflow burden, response times, and prevention adherence.

future_directions.title: Benchmark alternative time-series and deep learning approaches against XGBoost
future_directions.rationale: While XGBoost performed well, exploring LSTM, GRU, or transformer-based architectures may capture complex temporal dependencies. Conduct head-to-head comparisons on identical data splits, focusing on AUROC, calibration, interpretability, and computation time, to determine if more complex models offer meaningful gains with acceptable trade-offs in deployment complexity.

future_directions.title: Establish continuous learning and model maintenance pipelines
future_directions.rationale: Enable ongoing performance monitoring, drift detection, and periodic retraining as new data accrue across sites. Implement automated labeled data collection, versioning, and governance to ensure the model remains accurate and clinically relevant over time. Steps include setting drift thresholds, scheduling incremental retraining, and validating post-deployment performance quarterly.

future_directions.title: Conduct cost-benefit analyses and ROI studies for ML-based HAPI prevention
future_directions.rationale: Quantify economic impact, including potential reductions in HAPI-related costs, staffing implications, and return on investment from earlier interventions. Design studies to compare standard care versus ML-guided prevention strategies, incorporating sensitivity analyses for varying HAPI incidence and implementation scales.
